See also: Panorama, panoráma, panoramă, panoramą, and Panoramą

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
panorama
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From pan- (“all”) +‎ Ancient Greek ὅρᾱμᾰ (hórāmă, “view”). Coined by Robert Barker (painter) in 1792.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˌpæn.əˈɹæm.ə/, /ˌpæn.əˈɹɑː.mə/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (US, Canada) IPA(key): /ˌpæn.əˈɹæm.ə/, [ˌpɛən.əˈɹɛəm.ə], /ˌpæn.əˈɹɑː.mə/, [ˌpɛən.əˈɹɑː.mə]
    • Audio (US):(file)
  • (General Australian) IPA(key): /ˌpæn.əˈɹæm.ə/, /ˌpæn.əˈɹaː.mə/
  • Rhymes: -ɑːmə

Noun

[edit]

panorama (plural panoramas or panoramata)

  1. An unbroken view of an entire surrounding area.
    • 1963, Margery Allingham, “Foreword”, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
      He stood transfixed before the unaccustomed view of London at night time, a vast panorama which reminded him […] of some wood engravings far off and magical, in a printshop in his childhood.
  2. A picture or series of pictures representing a continuous scene.
  3. (figuratively) A comprehensive survey.

Usage notes

[edit]
  • The plural form panoramata is very rare.

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
panorama
Wikipedia pl
panorama sense 1
panorama sense 3
panorama sense 4
panorama sense 5

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism; compare English panorama, French panorama, German Panorama, ultimately from Ancient Greek ὅραμα (hórama).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pa.nɔˈra.ma/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ama
  • Syllabification: pa‧no‧ra‧ma
  • Homophone: Panorama

Noun

[edit]

panorama f (related adjective panoramowy)

  2. panorama (unbroken view of an entire surrounding area) [with genitive ‘of what’]
    Synonym: perspektywa
    Hypernym: widok
  3. (film, literature) panorama (comprehensive presentation of an issue in a literary work or film) [with genitive ‘of what’]
    Hypernym: opis
  5. (painting) panorama (large-scale painting on canvas, usually depicting a landscape or battle scene) [with genitive ‘of what’]
    Hypernyms: malowidło, obraz
  7. (photography) panorama (photograph depicting an extensive view, usually viewed from an elevated position) [with genitive ‘of what’]
    Hypernyms: fotografia, zdjęcie
  9. skyline (horizontal silhouette of a city or building against the sky) [with genitive ‘of what’]
